full_original_page:
# 1004. Hörmander densities for equations driven by measurable Markovian rough paths

**Area:** Rough paths and singular stochastic equations
**Status:** 🟡 PARTIAL
**Last checked:** 2026-10-30

## Problem statement

Let $`d,e\ge1`$, $`N\ge2`$, and let $`G^N(\mathbb R^d)`$ be the free step-$`N`$ nilpotent Lie group with its horizontal left-invariant generators $`U_1,\ldots,U_d`$ and Haar measure $`\lambda`$. Let $`a:G^N(\mathbb R^d)\to\mathrm{Sym}_d`$ be measurable, with

```math
\Lambda^{-1}|\xi|^2\le \xi^Ta(x)\xi\le\Lambda|\xi|^2
\quad(x\in G^N(\mathbb R^d),\ \xi\in\mathbb R^d)
```


for some finite $`\Lambda\ge1`$. Let $`\mathbf X=\mathbf X^{a,x_0}`$ be the canonical Markovian rough-path diffusion of Chevyrev–Ogrodnik §1.1, associated with the closure in $`L^2(\lambda)`$ of

```math
\mathcal E(f,g)=\int\sum_{i,j=1}^d a_{ij}(x)(U_if)(x)(U_jg)(x)\,d\lambda(x),
\qquad f,g\in C_c^\infty(G^N(\mathbb R^d)).
```


Interpret this diffusion as a geometric rough path, as in the cited source. Let $`V_1,\ldots,V_d\in C_b^\infty(\mathbb R^e;\mathbb R^e)`$, and suppose their iterated Lie brackets span $`\mathbb R^e`$ at every point. For arbitrary deterministic initial states $`x_0\in G^N(\mathbb R^d)`$ and $`y_0\in\mathbb R^e`$, solve

```math
dY_t=\sum_{i=1}^d V_i(Y_t)\,d\mathbf X_t^i,\qquad Y_0=y_0.
```


Must the law of $`Y_t`$ be absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure on $`\mathbb R^e`$ for every $`t>0`$?

This is the full-dimensional, bounded-smooth-vector-field form of the question in Chevyrev–Ogrodnik, Remark 3.11. The source also asks the corresponding question on the orbit generated by the vector fields. No smoothness of $`a`$, constant rank of brackets of length greater than $`N`$, or smoothness of the resulting density is required here.

## Application

The equation describes a nonlinear system driven by diffusion through a medium whose local covariance can be merely measurable. A density permits probabilities for the system's state to be represented by integration, even when ordinary stochastic differential-equation formulas requiring smooth noise coefficients are unavailable. The question tests whether the usual bracket condition alone supplies that property for this class of rough inputs.

## References

- I. Chevyrev and M. Ogrodnik, *A support and density theorem for Markovian rough paths*, Electronic Journal of Probability **23** (2018), paper 56, 1–16. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1214/18-EJP184); [arXiv v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1701.03002v2), model in §§1–1.1 and 3.2; Remark 3.11, PDF p.12.
- G. Yang, *A Version of Hörmander's Theorem for Markovian Rough Paths*, Potential Analysis **60** (2024), 173–195, published online 18 October 2022. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11118-022-10046-5); [arXiv v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2005.09192v4), Assumptions 1.4–1.7 and Theorem 1.8, PDF pp.3–4.

## Status review


**Known cases:** The coefficients are arbitrary measurable functions of the entire free group. The 2024 smooth-density theorem imposes smooth first-level coefficients and extra derivative nondegeneracy; the original constant-rank criterion is stronger than ordinary spanning.

**Remaining target:** Resolve the full Problem statement with its stated quantifiers and hypotheses; the restricted advances discussed here do not settle that target.

### Online recheck, 2026-10-30

The coefficients are arbitrary measurable functions of the entire free group. The 2024 smooth-density theorem imposes smooth first-level coefficients and extra derivative nondegeneracy; the original constant-rank criterion is stronger than ordinary spanning.

The primary-source formulation and earlier dated status review are retained below. Fresh query results and hypothesis comparisons are recorded in the [integration register](../research/further-integration-2026-10-30/README.md). This is a bounded literature and announcement search, not a guarantee of continued openness or certification of every cited proof.

Checked 17 October 2026. Chevyrev–Ogrodnik prove marginal density under an additional constant-rank condition on brackets of lengths greater than $`N`$. Their Remark3.11 explicitly asks whether ordinary Hörmander spanning suffices. Yang's later smooth-density theorem assumes smooth first-level noise coefficients and an additional derivative nondegeneracy condition. It does not cover arbitrary measurable coefficients depending on the full group element.

Current proof, counterexample and announcement searches found no complete resolution. The closest AIM match concerns kinetic PDE control, rather than marginal laws of rough differential equations. All-status AIM, current OpenAI overview and FURTHER checks found no duplicate. Prove2Me windows concerned unrelated uses of Hörmander references and marginal density. Exact version, source-reading and access limits are in the [source packet](../FURTHER_problems/_tracking/parallel/rough-filtering/markovian-density-held.json) and [independent review](../FURTHER_problems/_tracking/markovian-density-coordinator-review.json). Negative searches do not certify openness.
